items.title: HN: Learning to solve hard problems in RL for LLMs by never giving up
items.why: Discusses a new RL exploration/curriculum technique for getting LLMs to solve hard problems, relevant to RL training methods researchers track for reward hacking and capability gains.

items.title: Beyond the Name: Demographic Leakage in De-Identified R\'esum\'es and Evaluation Artifacts in LLM Bias Audits
items.why: Shows that removing declared-language fields doesn't fix demographic leakage in de-identified resume bias audits across 9 open-weight models, exposing a methodological flaw relevant to LLM bias evaluation design.

items.title: HN: Gemini 3.8 Live and 3.8 Live Extended Thinking
items.why: Announcement of Gemini 3.8 Live and Extended Thinking variants, a new frontier model release worth tracking for capability and eval comparisons.

items.title: Rewarding Reasoning, Not Answers: Fixing and Bounding Test-Time Reinforcement Learning on Medical QA
items.why: Demonstrates that test-time RL with majority-vote pseudo-labels collapses output diversity on medical QA despite math gains, a concrete reward-hacking/RL failure mode relevant to RL researchers.

items.title: HN: 1Password's AI patching benchmark is misleading
items.why: Discussion critiquing a specific AI code-patching benchmark's methodology, relevant to evaluating benchmark validity and potential gaming.

items.title: Test-Time Unlearning via Sparse Autoencoder
items.why: Proposes test-time unlearning via sparse autoencoders as an alternative to weight-editing methods, directly relevant to mechanistic interpretability applications for knowledge removal.

items.title: HN: GPT-5.6 Luna vs. GPT-6 Astra: Is a $1.20 Model Good Enough for Code Review?
items.why: Community comparison of GPT-5.6 Luna vs GPT-6 Astra on code review tasks including cost-effectiveness, providing informal benchmark evidence on frontier model capability tradeoffs.

items.title: LSREP: A Longitudinal State-Replay Protocol for Evaluating Conversational Memory, with ICE v2 as an Audited Local-First Architecture
items.why: Introduces a longitudinal replay protocol for evaluating how conversational memory systems accumulate, age, and revise state over time, a new eval methodology beyond single-turn QA.

items.title: ImpossibleRubrics: Stress-Testing Generated Rubrics as Reward Signals
items.why: Stress-tests LLM-generated rubrics used as RL reward signals against adversarial optimization on impossible tasks, directly probing reward hacking vulnerabilities in rubric-based RL.

items.title: R3: Robust Rubric-Agnostic Reward Models
items.why: Proposes rubric-agnostic reward models aimed at improving controllability and interpretability of reward signals, relevant to RL alignment and reward hacking research.

items.title: There Is More to Refusal in Large Language Models than a Single Direction
items.why: Challenges the single-direction theory of refusal in LLMs, showing geometrically distinct directions for different refusal categories, a core mechanistic interpretability finding on safety behavior.

items.title: Toward Robust LLM-Based Judges: Taxonomic Bias Evaluation and Debiasing Optimization
items.why: Presents a taxonomy of biases in LLM-as-judge evaluation across generative and discriminative formulations plus a debiasing optimization method, directly useful for improving eval reliability.

items.title: MiCRo: Mixture Modeling and Context-aware Routing for Personalized Preference Learning
items.why: Proposes mixture-model reward modeling with context-aware routing to replace the single global Bradley-Terry reward, directly relevant to RLHF reward hacking and preference learning research.

items.title: HoloAegis: Frozen Representation, Topological Inference --- Minimally Parametric Safety Manifolds and Their Capability Boundaries for LLM Guardrails
items.why: Introduces a training-free, geometry-based guardrail framework operating on frozen LLM representations, offering an interpretability-flavored alternative to fine-tuned or LLM-judge safety filters.

items.title: FVSpec: Real-World Property-Based Tests as Lean Challenges
items.why: New benchmark translating real-world property-based tests into Lean formal verification challenges, giving a concrete eval harness for assessing LLM/agent code verification ability.

items.title: Skill-based Agentic Evaluation for Real-time Data Science Tasks
items.why: Proposes an agentic evaluation framework for data-science LLM agents using live data and executable ground truth instead of static LLM-as-judge scoring, directly relevant to eval harness design.

items.title: ResLRP: The Role of Residual Cancellation in Attribution Instability in Vision Transformers
items.why: Identifies residual-connection cancellation as a cause of unstable/unfaithful LRP attributions in Vision Transformers, a mechanistic interpretability method fix relevant to attribution research more broadly.

items.title: Attention is All You Need Until You Need Retention
items.why: Proposes a persistent 'Retention Layer' memory mechanism for Transformers plus a social-learning framing for what agents should retain across sessions, relevant to human-AI interaction and agent memory design.

items.title: Domain-Specific Jargon in Large Language Models: A Comparative Analysis between General-Purpose and Specialist Models
items.why: Introduces two new medical jargon evaluation benchmarks probing how parametric knowledge of domain terms is encoded in general vs specialist LLMs, relevant to eval design and interpretability of knowledge encoding.

items.title: Same Patient, Different Order: Action-Level Reliability of Clinical LLM Agents Under Repeated Runs
items.why: Proposes action-level (not just verdict-level) reliability testing for clinical LLM agents across repeated runs on MedAgentBench, exposing a blind spot in single-attempt agent benchmarking methodology.

items.title: When Consistency Does Not Mean Reliability: Evaluating Local LLM Judges Against Human Ratings
items.why: Empirically tests whether consistent LLM-as-a-Judge scores actually correlate with human ratings using LLaMA-3-8B and Qwen2.5-7B judges, directly informing judge-based eval reliability.

items.title: Policy Loopholes in Agent Evaluation: When Policy Ambiguity Masquerades as Agent Error
items.why: Introduces a taxonomy of policy ambiguity in agent benchmarks like tau2-bench, showing that many 'agent errors' are actually artifacts of underspecified gold policies, a methodological critique relevant to agent eval validity.

items.title: Optimizing Sparse Outcomes Through Dense Behavioral Signals via Value-Guided Preference Distillation
items.why: Proposes a multi-head value model trained on dense behavioral signals to optimize long-horizon dialogue while explicitly addressing reward hacking, directly relevant to RL/reward hacking research.

items.title: A primer on evaluation methods for large language models in healthcare
items.why: A review synthesizing evaluation methodologies and challenges specific to deploying LLMs in healthcare, useful reference for eval researchers thinking about domain-specific validity issues.

items.title: One Example Is Enough to Pass Fairness Benchmarks: Rethinking Fairness Evaluation for Aligned LLMs
items.why: Shows fairness benchmarks like BBQ can be gamed with a single GRPO-trained example, a direct critique of benchmark robustness relevant to eval methodology and reward hacking.

items.title: Artificial entrepreneurial cognition: Locating and causally steering an opportunity recognition dial inside large language models (LLMs)
items.why: Uses causal steering/probing techniques to locate an 'opportunity recognition' direction in LLM internals, a mech-interp style method applied to a novel behavioral construct.

items.title: Can We Trust the Judges? Validation of Factuality Evaluation Methods via Answer Perturbation
items.why: Introduces a meta-evaluation framework that stress-tests factuality metrics via controlled answer corruptions, directly addressing whether current LLM eval judges are trustworthy.

items.title: K-Bench: a clinically calibrated benchmark for evaluating large language models in high-risk mental health conversations
items.why: A clinician-calibrated benchmark testing 125 model configurations on high-risk mental health conversations, a concrete new safety-relevant eval harness for human-AI interaction research.

items.title: The Limits of Reference-Free Speech Quality Metrics as Evaluators and Rewards on Modern Text-to-Speech
items.why: Empirically tests whether reference-free TTS quality metrics (used both as evaluators and as RL reward signals) actually track human preference, relevant to reward hacking and reward-model validity concerns.

items.title: Does Reasoning Improve Psychological Depth in Large Language Models? It Depends on Who's Judging
items.why: Shows that LLM-judge validity for scoring psychological depth in stories breaks down depending on which judge/human rater is used, a concrete case study on LLM-as-judge reliability.

items.title: Clean Scores, Buried Evidence, and Confident Wrong: A Receipt-Based Audit of Frontier Agentic QA
items.why: Introduces a controlled agentic QA audit showing buried evidence degrades accuracy and inflates confident wrong answers, a concrete eval methodology for measuring miscalibration and reward hacking in tool-using agents.

items.title: Lost-in-the-Middle in Long-Text Generation: Synthetic Dataset, Evaluation Framework, and Mitigation
items.why: Presents a synthetic dataset and evaluation framework for measuring and mitigating lost-in-the-middle effects in long-input-to-long-output generation, a reusable benchmark for long-context eval.

items.title: Who Benchmarks the Benchmarks? Towards Comprehensive Evaluation of Commonsense Reasoning Benchmarks
items.why: A meta-evaluation of commonsense reasoning benchmarks like HellaSwag exposing validity issues, directly relevant to researchers assessing benchmark reliability.

items.title: Confident Rankings with Fewer Items: Adaptive LLM Evaluation with Continuous Scores
items.why: Extends IRT-based adaptive testing to continuous LLM-as-judge scores, offering a more efficient benchmark evaluation method applicable beyond binary MCQ setups.

items.title: On the Interpretability of Whisper Encodings Using Sparse Autoencoders
items.why: Applies sparse autoencoders to Whisper's encoder to find monosemantic features, extending mechanistic interpretability methods beyond text transformers into ASR systems.

items.title: Data Attribution of Emergent Misalignment with Persona Features
items.why: Traces emergent misalignment persona features back to specific pre-training documents, directly extending mechanistic interpretability work on why fine-tuning causes broad misalignment.

items.title: What's the Catch? Evaluating Temporal Consistency in Vision-Language Models
items.why: Introduces TimeCatch, an anomaly-detection-based benchmark for probing whether VLMs actually capture temporal structure in video, a reusable eval method.

items.title: To See is Not to Master: Teaching LLMs to Use Private Libraries for Code Generation
items.why: Shows retrieval-augmented private-library API documentation injection is insufficient for code generation and proposes a training method, relevant to LLM capability evaluation on realistic coding tasks.

items.title: Transcoders Trace Visual Grounding and Hallucinations in Vision-Language Models
items.why: Applies transcoders (function-centric interpretability tool) to trace how VLMs transform visual inputs into text and diagnose hallucinations, a new mech interp technique for multimodal models.

items.title: Root-Cause Attribution Is a Search Problem: Continual Search for Long-Horizon Agent Failures
items.why: Frames root-cause attribution of long-horizon agent failures as a search problem, offering a new automated diagnostic method relevant to agent evaluation and debugging at scale.

items.title: Identity Is More Than Recall: A Benchmark for Persistent Identity in Deployed AI Agents
items.why: Introduces PAI-Bench, a provider-neutral benchmark separating recall from behavioral enactment of identity contracts in deployed agents, a new eval methodology for persistent agent identity.

items.title: Safety Signals to Verify NetOps Agents with Action-Level Granularity
items.why: Proposes action-level safety verification signals for autonomous NetOps agents, a new methodology for evaluating long-horizon agent reliability relevant to agent eval/reward-hacking concerns.

items.title: DynSTEER: Dynamic Stage-wise Trajectory Evaluation and Execution-time Review for Agents
items.why: DynSTEER introduces a stage-wise trajectory evaluation method with execution-time review to localize agent errors beyond terminal-only or single-reference matching, a new agent eval harness approach.

items.title: GAUGE: When Not to Trust LLM-as-a-Judge in User-Simulated Evaluation of Task-Oriented Agents
items.why: Introduces GAUGE, a protocol testing whether LLM-judge-based agent evaluation gates actually correlate with grounded verifiable rewards, directly relevant to LLM-as-judge reliability research.

items.title: SynthSentry: Detecting Synthetic Data Contamination in Language Model Training Data
items.why: Proposes a corpus-level signal to detect synthetic/model-generated contamination in training data before training, relevant to data quality and model collapse concerns.

items.title: Zipbench: Low-Cost Framework for Compressing Comprehensive Benchmarks of Large Language Models
items.why: Presents a low-cost method to compress large benchmark suites into representative subsets without requiring costly per-sample results from many LLMs, an adoptable benchmark compression technique.

items.title: Tasks over Application Manuals: Revealing Gaps in Long-Horizon Procedural Reasoning for Language Models
items.why: New long-horizon procedural reasoning benchmark built from application manuals that exposes gaps beyond short-horizon multi-hop reasoning tests.

items.title: Harness or Model? Isolating the Harness Effect in Agentic Coding with a Contamination-Controlled Private Suite
items.why: Uses a contamination-controlled private coding suite to isolate how much agentic coding performance depends on the harness versus the underlying model, directly informing eval harness methodology.

items.title: MAxBench: A Multinomial Concept Recovery Benchmark
items.why: Introduces a benchmark for recovering multinomial (non-binary) concepts in activation space, directly relevant to steering and interpretability research beyond simple linear-direction concepts.

items.title: MP-Bench: Evaluating Voice Agents as a Multiparty Conversation Participant
items.why: New benchmark evaluating voice agents in multi-party conversations, extending human-AI interaction evaluation beyond dyadic chat settings.

items.title: Limits of LLM Text Detectors in Education
items.why: Studies failure modes of LLM-generated text detectors specifically in the nuanced case of partial/assisted writing, relevant to eval methodology for LLM detection tools.

items.title: KoSimpleQA: A Korean Factuality Benchmark with an Analysis of Reasoning LLMs
items.why: New factuality benchmark (938 Q&A pairs) targeting Korean cultural knowledge with analysis of reasoning models, a genuine SimpleQA-style eval extension rather than mere localization repackaging.

items.title: MMGR: Multi-Modal Generative Reasoning Benchmark and Evaluation
items.why: New benchmark testing whether multimodal generative models preserve physical/logical/spatial constraints, probing genuine reasoning vs. surface plausibility in generation.

items.title: SAEExplainer: Interpreting SAE Features with Activation-Guided Preference Optimization
items.why: Proposes a closed-loop method using activation-guided preference optimization to generate and refine SAE feature explanations, advancing mechanistic interpretability tooling.

items.title: When Auditors Fabricate: Batch-Size Degradation and Confident Hallucination in LLM Detection of Planted Document Contamination
items.why: Empirical study showing LLMs used as document-quality auditors confidently hallucinate detections of planted contamination, relevant to LLM-as-judge reliability research.

items.title: Countdown-Code: A Testbed for Studying The Emergence and Generalization of Reward Hacking in RLVR
items.why: Introduces Countdown-Code, a controlled RLVR testbed for studying emergence and generalization of reward hacking, directly relevant to reward hacking research.

items.title: Capable but Careless: Do Computer-Use Agents Follow Contextual Integrity?
items.why: Introduces AgentCIBench, an evaluation harness testing whether computer-use agents respect contextual integrity/privacy norms across applications, relevant to agent eval and human-AI interaction.

items.title: EvoHarnessBench: Can Your Agents Keep Pace with an Evolving Harness?
items.why: Introduces EvoHarnessBench, a benchmark for testing agent robustness as their tool/skill/agent harness evolves, a new agentic eval harness with adoption potential.

items.title: SAEScientist-Bench: Can AI Agents Conduct Autonomous SAE Interpretability Research?
items.why: SAEScientist-Bench tests whether AI agents can autonomously conduct sparse-autoencoder interpretability research, directly relevant to mechanistic interpretability tooling and automation.

items.title: Beyond Solver Verdicts: Generative Reward Models for Autoformalization
items.why: Proposes generative reward models to catch verdict-preserving-unfaithful autoformalizations, relevant to reward model design and reward hacking in verification pipelines.

items.title: SoK: Rethinking Jailbreaking in the Era of Agentic AI: Attacks, Defenses, and Practical Consideration
items.why: Systematizes jailbreak attacks and defenses specifically for agentic AI systems with tool use and memory, relevant to safety evaluation of modern agentic models.

items.title: EvoRS: On-Policy Self-Evolution of Reward Systems for Open-Ended Reinforcement Learning
items.why: Proposes on-policy self-evolving reward systems to counter reward hacking and discriminability collapse in rubric-based RL, directly relevant to reward hacking research.

items.title: Can We Trust LLM Judges: A Study of Capability-Dependent Biases and Multi-Judge Ensemble for Bias Calibration
items.why: Empirically maps capability-dependent biases in LLM-as-judge absolute scoring across 36 judge-examinee pairs and proposes multi-judge ensemble calibration, directly actionable for eval harness design.

items.title: Reality Is the Final Verifier: On Two Key Gaps in Agentic Software Engineering
items.why: Analyzes gaps between test-suite verification and real deployment correctness in agentic coding, relevant to designing more robust SWE-agent benchmarks.

items.title: Debiasing as a Measurement Intervention: Calibrated Ties and Resolution Loss in LLM-as-a-Judge Evaluation
items.why: Introduces TraceJudgeBench, a diagnostic benchmark showing that instructing judges to ignore presentation cues damages measurement resolution, a concrete new eval tool for RAG/agent judge auditing.

items.title: TREAT: Evaluating Access to Formal Knowledge across Equivalent Mathematical Representations
items.why: Introduces TREAT, a benchmark testing whether LLMs recognize theorems across equivalent formal representations, a novel formal-reasoning eval method.

items.title: Mr.LHDR: A Benchmark for Multimodal Real-World Long-Horizon Deep Research Agents
items.why: Mr.LHDR is a new benchmark for evaluating multimodal deep-research agents on long-horizon, dependency-heavy tasks, relevant to agent eval harness design.

items.title: Who Judges the Judges? A Chinese Safety QA Benchmark for Evaluating LLM Responses and Safety Judges
items.why: C-SafeQA is a new Chinese safety benchmark evaluating both LLM responses and safety judge models, directly relevant to LLM-as-judge and safety eval methodology.

items.title: HN: Astra and Fable still hack on simple variants of alignment evals from 2025
items.why: Discussion of Astra and Fable models still succeeding at gaming simplified variants of 2025 alignment evals, directly relevant to tracking reward hacking and eval robustness.

items.title: Mr.LHDR: A Benchmark for Multimodal Real-World Long-Horizon Deep Research Agents
items.why: Introduces Mr.LHDR, a new multimodal benchmark specifically testing long-horizon, dependency-heavy deep research agent behavior beyond existing medium-horizon eval sets.

items.title: Overview of the NLPCC 2026 Shared Task 11: Agent-Based Experiment Reproduction from Scientific Papers
items.why: NLPCC shared task introducing AgentActionBench, a new benchmark for evaluating LLM agents' ability to reproduce scientific experiments, relevant as an agent-eval harness.

items.title: BenchShield: Formal Model-Backed Instrumentation for Reward Integrity in LLM-Agent Evaluation Infrastructure
items.why: Proposes formal-model-backed instrumentation to detect and prevent reward hacking in interactive LLM-agent benchmark infrastructure, directly relevant to reward-hacking research.

items.title: New Evidence, Same Choice: Testing Physical Experiment Selection in Vision Language Models
items.why: New benchmark testing whether VLMs know when they need additional physical measurements versus can answer from existing evidence, a reasoning/eval method for vision-language models.

items.title: Defining AI Agents: A Compendium of Criteria, Metrics, and Benchmarks
items.why: Survey compendium proposing structured criteria, metrics, and benchmarks for defining 'AI agent' across five dimensions, useful reference for standardizing agent evaluation.

items.title: An Open Recipe for IMO Gold: Training Nemotron for Olympiad Mathematics
items.why: Describes an open post-training and test-time-compute recipe (SFT+RL+verification) that pushed Nemotron to IMO-gold-level olympiad proof generation, relevant to frontier model and RL reasoning capability tracking.
